items.title: Elvin Jones — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: He was a wonderful guy, just a sweetheart. He and John got together and they were like two peas in a pod.

ctx.x: Now Coltrane, as a bandleader, began inviting other folks into the band to perform or record. Probably one of the earliest ones, and the most memorable, is Eric Dolphy coming in and playing. Can you describe that experience?

Yes cause I knew Eric Dolphy, I saw him when he played with Charlie Mingus in that group. Mingus had some very unusual arrangements, and it took people with the skill of people like Eric Dolphy to play Mingus’ music. Nobody else could do it, because he had such a command over his instrument that he could play just about anything he wanted.
How was Eric as a person?
